full_judgment:
Ms. Nazmun Ara Sultana, J:- This Rule was issued calling in question the entire proceeding of Artha Execution Case No.1790 of 2003 of Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Chittagong and also the order No.32 dated 23.3.2004 and order No.41 dated 17.5.2005 passed in that Artha Execution Case. 

2. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of this rule, in short, are that the respondent No.3-P Public Bank Limited filed Money suit No.21 of 1983 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1'1 Court, Chittagong against this petitioner for recovery of loan money. The said suit was subsequently re-numbered as Money suit No.28 of 1984 and was decreed exparte by the judgment and order dated 14.7.1984. The decree holder bank then put that decree in execution in Money execution Case No.2 of 1984. This petitioner along with others filed a miscellaneous case being Misc. Case No. 62 of 1986 under order 9 rule 13 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside that exparte decree, but the said mist case was ultimately rejected by the order dated 14.12.1987. However the Money Execution Case No.2 of 1984 was subsequently dismissed for default by the order dated 3.10.1992. Thereafter on 8.2.99 the decree-holder bank filed a fresh execution case being Money Execution Case No.1 of 1999. The said money execution case No.1 of 1999 was subsequently transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, 1970 of 2003. In that Artha Execution Case No.1790 of 2003, on the prayer of the decree holder bank, the impugned order no.32 dated 23.3.2004 was passed issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner. Thereafter, this petitioner appeared in that execution case and filed an application praying for rejection of the execution case on the ground of limitation and also for recalling the warrant of arrest issued against him. By the other impugned order no.41 dated 17.5.2005 the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat concerned rejected the said prayer of the petitioner. 

3. The petitioner thereafter has come to this court with this writ petition and obtained the rule. 

4. Mr. Shah Md. Munir Sharif, the learned advocate appearing, for the writ petitioner has mainly argued that the execution case in question is hopelessly barred by limitation and as such the entire proceeding as well as the impugned orders are illegal. To elaborate his argument the learned advocate has submitted that admittedly the decree in question was passed on 14.7.1984 and thereafter the 1st execution case was filed on 26.11.1984. This execution case was dismissed for default on 3.10.1992 and thereafter the execution case in question i.e. the 2nd execution case was filed on 8.2.1999. The learned advocate has pointed out that as per Article 182 of the Limitation Act this 2nd execution case had to be filed within 3 years from the date of dismissal of the 1st execution case and as per section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure within 12 years from the date of passing of the decree in order to save the limitation. The learned advocate has contended the since the 2nd execution case in question was filed long after expiry of 12 years from the date of passing of decree and also long after expiry of 3 years from the date of dismissal of the first execution case it is hopelessly barred by limitation. 

5. We have considered the argument of the learned advocate for the petitioner and examined the Writ petition and the papers annexed thereto. Admittedly the present execution case was filed long 8 years after dismissal of the 1st execution case and long 16 years after passing of the decree. The learned advocate appearing for the respondent No.3 decree-holder bank also has frankly conceded this fact that the execution case in question has not been filed within the time prescribed in Article 182 of the Limitation Act and in section 48 of the Code of Civil Procedure. So, in this circumstances without any further discussion it may be said that the execution case in question being hopelessly barred by limitation is unlawful and as such the impugned orders passed in this execution case also are of no legal effect. 

6. In the circumstances the rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. It is declared that the proceeding of Artha Execution Case No.1, Chittagong as well as the order No.32 dated 23.3.2004 and the order no.41 dated 17.5.2005 passed in that Artha Execution Case are unlawful and of no legal effect. 

End.
